insights.concise_text: Because available annotated data is very limited and additional training data has the biggest impact on improving performance, the paper's artificial error generation methods address a key bottleneck for error detection.

triple.subject: artificial error generation methods
triple.object: limited annotated data bottleneck

insights.concise_text: The SMT framework that trains a model to translate from correct into incorrect sentences is implemented by treating error-corrected sentences as source and original learner sentences as target.

triple.subject: SMT framework
triple.object: error-corrected sentences as source and original learner sentences as target

insights.concise_text: The pattern-based method extends Felice2014a by relaxing the restriction to only five error types, and its all-error-type coverage is credited with consistently improving performance.

triple.subject: pattern-based method
triple.object: Felice2014a by generating all error types

insights.concise_text: Felice2014a's five error types cover only 35.74% of all errors in the CoNLL 2014 training dataset, motivating the paper's all-types AEG methods that consistently improve performance.

triple.subject: 35.74% coverage of CoNLL 2014 training dataset errors
triple.object: need for all-types AEG methods

insights.concise_text: Automatically labeled data from Levenshtein-aligned alternative sentence versions is used to train error detection models, whose performance is substantially improved by artificially generated data.

triple.subject: Levenshtein-aligned automatically labeled data
triple.object: error detection models trained with only manual annotation

insights.concise_text: The combination of both AEG methods gives an absolute improvement of 4.3% in INLINEFORM0 and is identified as Ann+PAT+MT, the best overall system on all datasets.

triple.subject: Ann+PAT+MT
triple.object: all datasets with an absolute improvement of 4.3% in INLINEFORM0

insights.concise_text: Because the two frameworks learn to generate different types of errors, combining the pattern-based approach with the machine translation system gives the best overall performance on all datasets.

triple.subject: different error types learned by two frameworks
triple.object: best overall performance of Ann+PAT+MT on all datasets

insights.concise_text: The artificial data evaluated on FCE test data and two alternative annotations of the CoNLL 2014 Shared Task dataset was generated from 450K corrected FCE tokens and 270K English Vocabulary Profile tokens.

triple.subject: artificial data evaluation
triple.object: FCE test data and two alternative annotations of the CoNLL 2014 Shared Task dataset

insights.concise_text: The final combination system is significantly better than Felice2014a on all three datasets, supporting the claim that relaxing type restrictions and generating all types of errors consistently outperforms Felice2014a.

triple.subject: final combination system significance over Felice2014a
triple.object: all-types pattern-based method outperforming Felice2014a

insights.concise_text: The SMT system's n-best list of alternative translations enables multiple error-generated versions of the same input text, and showing such versions gives a distinct improvement on the development set.

triple.subject: SMT n-best list
triple.object: distinct improvement from multiple error-generated versions on the development set
